test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 16 Oct, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A cylinder with a radius of 12 cm and height of 38 cm is cut parallel to the base into two pieces of different sizes. The total surface area of the larger piece formed is 60% of the total surface area of the given cylinder. The smaller piece is melted and used to create a sphere. Find the radius (in cm) of the sphere.
solution:
**Given:**

Radius of Cylinder = 12 cm

Height = 38 cm

**Formula used:**

Surface area of the cylinder = 2πr(h + r)

Volume of the cylinder = πr²h

Volume of the sphere = (4/3)πr³

**Calculations:**

Total surface area of the cylinder = 2πr(h + r)

Let the height of the larger piece be H

Total surface area of the larger piece = 60% of 2πr(h + r)

⇒ 2πr² + 2πrH = 0.6 x 2πr(h + r) 

⇒ 2πr (r + H) = 0.6 x 2πr(h + r) 

⇒ (12 + H) = 0.6 x (38 + 12) 

⇒ 12 + H = 30 cm

⇒ H = 18 cm

So the height of the smaller piece = Hₛₘₐₗₗ = 38 - 18 = 20 cm

Volume of the smaller piece = Volume of the Sphere

⇒ πr2Hsmall = 4/3 πR³

⇒ (12)² x 20 = 4/3 R3

⇒ (8640) / 4 = R3

⇒ R = 6 times sqrt[3]{10} 

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**
